## Design

Agora supports multi-channel audio transmission and selective channel playback across the whole product line — the Linux SDK, Native SDK, Web SDK, and so on. This document specifically describes the design, implementation, features, and limitations of the multi-channel feature in the Web SDK.

The Web SDK and the corresponding Web VOS backend service implement the following functionality:

- On the web browser side, you can subscribe to and receive multi-channel audio streams sent from other platforms (such as the Linux SDK), and select one, two, or more of the audio channels to play back according to your business requirements.
- On the web browser side, you can send multi-channel audio streams; other platforms, including the Web SDK, can subscribe to and receive the audio streams.

## Implementation

The implementation modifies the Web VOS backend service and adds local multi-channel audio-related APIs, properties, and methods to the Web SDK, as well as remote multi-channel audio-related APIs, properties, and methods, to fulfill the multi-channel requirements. Its features are as follows:

- Adds support for 4-channel, 6-channel, and 8-channel multi-channel functionality; up to 8 channels are supported. 16-channel and similar requirements are not supported.
- The Web SDK can subscribe to and receive multi-channel audio streams and select any of the channels for playback; the specifics depend on the multi-channel standard and the conventions agreed with the sender.
- Due to limitations in Web Audio processing, Insertable Streams are currently used for channel selection, making it possible to play any combination of the 8 channels. The recommended Chrome version is Chrome 96; see the compatibility test results for details.

Example of channel-selective playback under the WebRTC multi-channel standard:

The web side now parses audio according to the standard multi-channel protocol. For example, selecting channel 2 (center channel) and channel 3 (LFE channel) plays back as stereo.

## Browser Compatibility of the Multi-channel Feature

The QA team's browser-side test results for the multi-channel feature are as follows:

- Chrome 94 and Chrome 95: support starts from these versions, but the relevant interfaces are not enabled by default.
- Chrome 96: official support starts from this version.
- Chrome 96 to Chrome 109: renegotiation after unsubscribing differs somewhat from the latest Chrome versions; this has now been made compatible.
- Chrome 110 to the latest version: fully supported.
- Safari and Firefox have various issues with the multi-channel feature and are not recommended for now.

Recommendation: To enable the multi-channel feature of the Web SDK, upgrade to Chrome 96 or a newer version. Safari and Firefox are not recommended.

## Multi-channel Integration Guide

### Multi-channel APIs, Properties, and Methods

For the concrete implementation, download the NPM package and check the `rtc-sdk_cn.d.ts` and `rtc-sdk_en.d.ts` files in it.

![rtc-sdk_en.d.ts in the NPM package](data:image/png;base64,)

### Local Multi-channel Audio

1. Create multi-channel audio: `createCustomAudioTrack`

```typescript
export interface CustomAudioTrackInitConfig {
  // *****
  channelCount?: number;
}
```

2. Property: `channelCount`

Gets the number of channels of the current track. This value is the one set at creation time, not obtained through the track interface; the SDK uses it internally to generate the `custom_payload_type` when publishing.

3. Method: `selectChannels(channels: number[], mode: "surround" | "stereo" | "mono" = "surround"): void;`

Sets the list of output channels.

Modes:

1. `surround`: surround sound; the standard multi-channel protocol.
2. `stereo`: mixes channels 0, 2, 4, 6, ... into the left channel and channels 1, 3, 5, ... into the right channel, so that the final result is a stereo effect.
3. `mono`: mixes all audio into a single channel; the output is stereo.

4. Method: `getVolumeLevels(channels?: number[]): number[];`

Gets the volume data of all channels, returned as an array.

### Remote Multi-channel Audio

1. Property: `channelCount`

Gets the number of channels of the current track. The value is generated from the `pt` value in the `on_add_audio_stream` signaling, rather than obtained from inside the track.

2. Method: `selectChannels(channels: number[], mode: "surround" | "stereo" | "mono" = "surround"): void;`

Sets the list of output channels.

Modes:

1. `surround`: surround sound; the standard multi-channel protocol.
2. `stereo`: mixes channels 0, 2, 4, 6, ... into the left channel and channels 1, 3, 5, ... into the right channel, so that the final result is a stereo effect.
3. `mono`: mixes all audio into a single channel; the output is stereo.

3. Method: `getVolumeLevels(channels?: number[]): number[];`

Gets the volume data of all channels, returned as an array.

### Reference Integration Code

Set the private parameter:

```javascript
AgoraRTC.setParameter("ENABLE_MULTIOPUS_CODEC", true);
```

Create and publish multi-channel audio:

```javascript
const audioTrack = await AgoraRTC.createMultiAudioTrack({
  mediaStreamTrack: getAudioBufferTrack(await createAudioBuffer(audioURL.value)),
  channelCount: 6,
});
await client.publish(audioTrack);
```

Receive and play multi-channel audio:

```javascript
const track = (await client.subscribe(user, kind)) as IRemoteTrack;
if (track && track.trackMediaType === "audio") {
  track.play();
  remoteAudioTrack = track;
}
```

Select channels and the audio rendering mode:

```javascript
const mode = "surround"
if (remoteAudioTrack) {
  const channels = [1,2];
  remoteAudioTrack.selectChannels(channels, mode);
}
```

Get volumes:

```javascript
// Volumes of all channels
remoteAudioTrack.getVolumeLevels();
// Volumes of the specified channels
remoteAudioTrack.getVolumeLevels([0, 1, 2]);
```

## Multi-channel Technical Details

### Audio Decoding

The following uses receiving 6-channel audio data as an example.

The receiver needs to add support for multiopus; its ORTC data is as follows:

```json
{
  "fmtp": {
    "parameters": {
      "channel_mapping": "0,1,2,3,4,5",
      "coupled_streams": "3",
      "num_streams": "3",
      "minptime": "10",
      "useinbandfec": "1"
    }
  },
  "payloadType": 123,
  "rtcpFeedbacks": [
    {
      "type": "transport-cc"
    },
    {
      "type": "nack"
    }
  ],
  "rtpMap": {
    "clockRate": 48000,
    "encodingName": "multiopus",
    "encodingParameters": 6
  }
}
```

You can directly set the `encodingParameters` value to the maximum of 8, which is compatible with 6-, 4-, and 2-channel audio.

The `parameters` attributes in fmtp are described below:

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| `channel_mapping` | Mapping between encoded channels and output channels |
| `coupled_streams` | Number of streams in which two channels are decoded into one stream |
| `num_streams` | Total number of streams |

Total channel count = `coupled_streams` + `num_streams`

### Channel Selection

Due to a Chrome bug (<https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=1116042>), WebAudio cannot be used for channel selection, so the implementation switches to Insertable Streams for channel selection.

```javascript
const track = __ARTC__.__TRACK_LIST__[0]._mediaStreamTrack
const trackProcessor = new MediaStreamTrackProcessor({ track });
const trackGenerator = new MediaStreamTrackGenerator({ kind: "audio" });
const transformer = new TransformStream({
  async transform(videoFrame, controller) {
    const { format, sampleRate, numberOfFrames, timestamp } = videoFrame;
    const nChannels = videoFrame.numberOfChannels;
    const buffer = new Float32Array(numberOfFrames * nChannels);
    const channels = window.channels || [0];
    channels.forEach((channel) => {
      const offset = numberOfFrames * channel;
      const samples = buffer.subarray(offset, offset + numberOfFrames);
      videoFrame.copyTo(samples, { planeIndex: channel, format });
      // getVolumeFromFloat32Array(samples);
    });
    videoFrame.close();
    controller.enqueue(
      new AudioData({
        format,
        sampleRate,
        numberOfFrames,
        numberOfChannels: nChannels,
        timestamp,
        data: buffer,
      })
    );
  },
});
trackProcessor.readable
  .pipeThrough(transformer)
  .pipeTo(trackGenerator.writable);
const au = document.createElement("audio");
const s = new MediaStream([trackGenerator]);
au.srcObject = s;
au.play();
```

Calculate the volume of a given channel:

```javascript
function getVolumeFromFloat32Array(audioData: Float32Array) {
  const sumSquare = audioData.reduce((prev, curr) => prev + curr * curr, 0);
  const meanSquare = sumSquare / audioData.length;
  const minLevel = 100.0;
  const level = Math.max(10.0 * Math.log10(meanSquare) + minLevel, 0);
  return level / minLevel;
}
```

## Pricing

Agora's multi-channel pricing has not changed for now. Although, cost-wise, the cost increases with the number of channels, due to R&D and product resource constraints the fee is the same as for normal dual-channel audio. This may change in the future.

## Limitations and Features

Agora multi-channel has restrictions on the Chrome version.

| NO. | Type | Limitations and Features |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Web | The recommended Chrome version is at least Chrome 96. |
| 2 | Web | Other browsers such as Safari and Firefox are not recommended. In a channel using the multi-channel feature, if a Safari or Firefox browser joins, the behavior is undefined — there may be no sound, or stereo playback may result. |
| 3 | Multi-channel capability negotiation | When Linux sends, if an endpoint that does not support multi-channel joins, the stream falls back to dual-channel. You can use the private parameter `"che.audio.codec_unfallback": [123, 124, 125]` to prevent the multi-channel feature from falling back. When the web sends, an unsupported endpoint joining does not trigger fallback, and that unsupported endpoint hears no sound. In other words, when using the multi-channel feature, you must ensure that all participants support multi-channel. |
